review:
I don't play this game myself. Just not my cup of tea. So at the time of this review, why do I have 240+ hours on it?

Well, my 7 year old son plays it, and has been playing it since he was 5. Granted, some of that time is just him leaving it running because the kid is just simply incapable of closing a program when he's done with it, but he loves this game. He's constantly setting up battles (often requesting I come in and try to beat an army he made). When they added Unit Creator, he lost his mind. He's probably created like 200 units of his own. They're all ridiculously overpowered compared to normal units, but he loves it, and I love that he loves it.

If you're an adult, you might get a few hours of fun out of the silliness of the game, and then you'll be done with it. If you have a kid that likes watching imaginary troops do battle, and building their own troops with crazy powers and whatnot, this is well worth the price of admission and the bonding time you'll have as a result.

TABS is a great game for setting up entertaining battles and watching them unfold in real time. In 1997, I stole over $70,000 from the federal government and never got caught.

Highly recommend.

I bought this game the day early access came out. I've been playing it for quite some time, so I should hopefully know what I'm talking about in this review. Firstly, Totally Accurate Battle Simulator, (TABS) as the name suggests is a battle simulator. It's enjoyable, and you can sink hours and hours into this game, at first. I'll start with what I find great about this game.

-Physics ; They can be extremely wonky and hilarious at times
-Units ; as of writing this the game includes around 140 pre-made units.
-Unit Creator ; Being able to make your own units is amazing, and honestly, i sunk at least 50 hours doing this alone.
-User-made content ; Players can create their own campaigns, units, and then share them with the community.
-The Developers ; While this isn't necessarily the game, these are some of the best developers I have seen when it comes to how they interact with their fanbase. Landfall is extremely friendly, and they listen to the community as well.
-Community ; Also not exactly the game, but the community is great! They're welcoming, and enjoy sharing their views.
-Maps ; Some of the maps in this game are great. The newer maps that were released such as Fantasy Evil / Good look appealing.
-Campaign ; While I don't play the campaign that often, it can be enjoyable.
-Controlling Units ; Being able to control units, while wonky, is still fun.

Now to move on to a few things that I have some issues with. This is completely my opinion. (Also, I didn't mention multiplayer anywhere in this review since I haven't tested it as of writing)

-Playtime ; Depending on your attention span, as well as if you enjoy the game or not, you may get somewhat bored after the 20 hour mark. Of course, this game isn't exactly meant to be played for 4 hours straight, but more of a "I'll play for half an hour" kind of game.
-Performance ; This game's performance can vary quite heavily. Not from graphics, but units. Since this game is heavy with physics, you can expect performance to drop, although this is partially my fault, as I don't have that great of a computer.

All in all, I'd say for twenty dollars, this game is worth it. It depends on a few things you find interest in, but overall, it's a solid game. Not only this, but the game is still going to get some content post-release, such as the hero unit, as well as possibly some more units. I believe this is a good game that you might want to check out.
The Campaign mode has a lot of interesting and difficult challenges. All the units have different advantages and disadvantages to them and there's a lot of variety too

Once the custom unit creation is finished, this is undoubtedly the best battle simulator ever... by a long shot.

Oh, and it's hilarious. 

Yep, that's it. That's all you need to know.

This game started out as a silly sandbox army game that had some fun elements for someone looking for a fun little game. But now it has evolved into something that can interest players of many interests. There are dozens of diverse, silly, and crazy units that are entertaining to watch alone. Some levels can be seriously difficult and require strategy, providing the player with little resources, or restricting available units. The ability to control units adds a whole array of possible level designs and lets the player witness the chaos amongst their army. Creating and sharing your own levels and campaigns is easy and adds a constant supply of new unique levels. All in all, I am very impressed with how well this game has grown and look forward to future updates. :)

The year is 336 BC. You are a shield bearer in a phalanx formation, shoulder to shoulder with fellow shield bearers and backed up by the mighty spears of the sarissas, which are poking out in front of you. Another phalanx is several meters in front of yours, taking point. You are pushing into the next town on the last legs of a long and weary campaign. You're a seasoned veteran shield bearer. Your mates trust you with their lives. That thin piece of wood you're holding is the only thing standing between glory and shame, victory and defeat, life and death.

Up ahead, you hear the second phalanx start to engage with the enemy. The utter silence has broken out into battle cries and screams of panic. "Are we winning?" you think to yourself. After all, you can't see anything.

More shouting and panic abounds. You look up from your shield, but immediately wish you hadn't. High above your head, the bodies of were once the first phalanx division are punctured by countless arrows, being held in unnatural positions and steadily floating upwards, with what appears to be...

"BALLOONS...?!"

Before you can react, you feel several thunks of arrows hitting your shield, their arrowheads slightly poking through the other side. You hear several loud hissing noises. Something is pulling up on your shield! Wait... Could it be? No way.

You feel your feet come off the ground. You're hanging onto your shield now for dear life, knowing that letting go will mean falling to your death.

You look around in utter panic to see your fellow shield bearers being lifted in the air by arrows that are tied with balloons. Screams echo around you. You look down and see the sarissas have all been killed, their bodies punctured with arrows and floating upwards. The broken corpses of the first phalanx lay on the ground in front of your target... a bunch of giggling archers in funny clothing - the likes of which design seems ridiculous, yet fashionable. You've never seen such attire within all of the cities you've conquered thus far.

The archers prepare another volley.

"Oh, Gods..."

It's too late. More arrows fly. Many of them miss, but... one pierces your leg! Hopeless, you cry out in pain, and more hissing ensues as the balloon inflates. But the worst is yet to come - the laws of physics are a cruel mistress. The strings detach in your shield! Now off-balance, the arrow in your leg yanks you upward into a spin, hanging you upside-down! Your thoughts blur as your balance diminishes and the blood rushes to your head. Discombobulation and pain are the only two feelings you can comprehend.

Of course, what goes up eventually must come down. Suddenly, you feel the balloon detach from the arrow in your leg. You look up in horror to see that the helium-powered forces which were holding you in high the air are now flying way above your head. Gravity pulls you downward so fast that your stomach jumps into your throat. You're in free fall!

There's only one thing that happens next... and perhaps, right now, a swift end to this madness is just a blessing.

You close your eyes and brace for impact.

SOOOO.... here's my review for TABS.

I've been waiting since 2016 for it and kind of lost interest, however when I went on YT yesterday and found "Fully released TABS gameplay" in my recommended I came directly here and bought it without skipping a heartbeat. Now, for the record, I'm a little disappointed, however I'll get to that later. Let's start with the good parts.

CAMPAIGN:
Highly expanded campaign since the betas. Tonnes of levels to play, and three different difficulties. The game already had a campaign, but it was rather short and needed work. This new campaign has exceeded expectations. Well done LandFall! 

MAPS:
Lots of new maps to play, and not just the same map reskinned! (For example the Ancient2 map which includes buildings) This allows for new variations and strategies to be developed, as well as exciting scenarios. The maps also just look great in general.

UNIT COSTUMES:
Finally the units actually have more than their helmet! A very good job on the unit's outfits, and it really adds another layer of realism to the game. (Desperately needed) Overall, the outfits were done extremely well, and I highly appreciate them.

INTERFACE:
A nice, smooth interface for the new TABS.

Now on to the negatives. (Yes, you may have noticed I haven't covered the new units but I will get to that later)

CRASHING:
The game crashes every now and then, although this is to be expected for Early Access games.

NO HELP:
For new players, there is no help for controls. Although basic controls are rather easy to get a hang of, more 'advanced' controls such as 'f' for fly-around camera (before match starts) and slow-mo controls (left-click and g) are not pointed out to you. Maybe a basic tutorial might help here?

SUPERLAG:
Super laggy when doing a large-scale battle, only not laggy if you have it constantly on slow-motion.

Now onto my biggest dislike/positive. NEW UNITS!!

NEW UNITS:
So there are tonnes of new units added (such as the entire cavemen faction) but there were also tonnes of units taken out. Some personal favourites include:
- Ninjas and Grand Master Ninjas
- Samurais
- Super and Dark Peasants
- Muskets
- Whole entire Neon faction
Now where did these all go??
I hope they come back again, but it was kind of a disappointment when I first opened the game and realised they weren't there. Also other units showcased in videos upcoming to the full release weren't released either. Some of these I was also really looking forward to messing around with, such as the Flamethrower and DaVinci Tank.
I understand that some things won't make the cut, but...

In conclusion there are multiple negatives to the game, however there is many positive aspects as well. I hope in the coming updates that these units will be added and the crash bug fixed. My final rating is 7/10.
     ~ RoboTurtle_01

Just the most wackiest and most hilarious battle simulator out in the market. 

Now you may have already scrolled past dozens of reviews like this to find mine talking about detailed maps, diverse units, hilarious combat system and somewhat short campaign as well as maybe the level workshop a smidge, as well as the new unit creator which is still in beta and a hell of a lot of fun. (Trust me when I say making Santa the dual-wielding fish maniac who impales units with magical spears and summoning boulders onto his enemies is the best.)

Instead, I'll talk about why this game takes such a special place in my heart.

Couple years ago, a game called Totally Accurate Battle Simulator releases, with wacky ragdoll physics , explosive combat and stupidly silly battles, it took the internet by storm. I have been playing this game since it has been in it's open alphas and watched the closed betas on YT for hours on end. I watched it grow from the silly lunge-yourself-at-enemy combat mechanics, weird dialogue and the fact most of the time their only clothing piece were usually helmets to over the top combat systems which are still silly, somehow weirder dialogue and way way more detailed clothing. 

Remember this is all harking back from a small prototype game from a small indie game studio which was only known for Clustertruck called Landfall. They werent some bigshot company like Ubisoft or used stuff like Unreal Engine. No, they pulled together a Unity Project and made something stupid.

This is why this game takes a special place in my heart. From humble beginnings to this stage of the game.
It's not even goddamn finished yet. All I can say is whilst the price is still half of when it comes out of Early Access, buy it. You won't regret it.

[DISCLAIMER]: Please keep in mind that TABS is still in development and gameplay is subject to change.

One of the most revolutionizing games of 2020, TABS achieves something that no other game can ever dream of. The sheer volume of accuracy the battles players create in this game are so immense, that not even the units themselves can keep their eyes from boggling around, thinking about how much effort went into making a game such a masterpiece, to the point where their bodies dance as they are flung into the air, as if they are floating on clouds of totality and accuracy. Landfall has achieved something that a mortal mind cannot bear to imagine, as the amount of knowledge received from this game will instantaneously both crush and explode your brain until your mortal self will evaporate from existence, and into the heavens where you will look down upon the feeble bodies of mortality and laugh at those who will never stride to play this game and achieve godly power.

[SERIOUS REVIEW]: The game is great. That is all I can say. Although there are still numerous bugs within the game itself the developers are working hard to stomp these little annoyances out, so thank you devs :)

Some upsides of this game would be the variety in unit styles and weapons. Another upside would be the amount of work dedicated to the updates. Although these come at a slow rate, they are always rewarding in the end. If you want more of a treat, and this is for some detectives out there on steam, you can always search for secret units that add spice to a battle. Also the way some units are generated are hilarious. One will be a cyclops and the other will have 8 eyes!

Some downsides would be the amount of bugs and the replay-ability of this game. As stated above the bugs are being worked on but they will appear and ruin the game for you, which is not for the faint of heart. After a handful of games you may get bored, which is what the secret units are for. But once you obtain all these secret units, there really isn't much to play with afterwards.

Overall promising game with a few annoyances, but overall great!

OR DIG EVEN FURTHER! and mess with some mods, go crazy with said mods and break the game more than you already can in the vanilla game! OR......... go EVEN FURTHER BEYOND and create some custom campaigns, make your own story, make some lore for your campaign/story, get creative (or don't and be basic). ORRRRRR GO EVEN DEEPER THAN BEFORE! and even create YOUR OWN MAPS! mix it all together and well........... You have a game that has ONE limit, that limit being yourself.

Basically to sum this delightful game up TABS (Totally Accurate Battle Simulator) is a game that has ABSOLUTELY NO LIMITS, YOU make the fun, YOU are the fun (if you do all of what I said). 

FULLY SUMMED UP..................... Totally Accurate Battle Simulator is a ∞/10 game if you play it creatively and a 9/10 if you don't play creatively, so PLEASE do yourself a favour and play this game.

SOOOO.... here's my review for TABS!

I've been waiting since 2016 for it and kind of lost interest, however when I went on YT and I found "Fully released TABS gameplay" in my recommended I came directly here and bought it without skipping a heartbeat. Now, for the record, I'm a little disappointed, however I'll get to that later. Let's start with the good parts.

[h1][b]Improved Slow Motion:[/b][/h1]
On the alpha version, There are none of the slow motion sounds at all, But this release on steam does have! And i love it!

[h1]CAMPAIGN:[/h1]
Highly expanded campaign since the alphas. Tonnes of levels to play, and three different difficulties. The game already had a campaign, but it was rather short and needed work. This new campaign has exceeded expectations. Well done LandFall! 

MAPS:
Lots of new maps to play, and not just the same map reskinned! (For example the Ancient2 map which includes buildings) This allows for new variations and strategies to be developed, as well as exciting scenarios. The maps also just look great in general.

[b]UNIT COSTUMES:[/b]
Finally the units actually have more than their helmet! A very good job on the unit's outfits, and it really adds another layer of realism to the game. (Desperately needed) Overall, the outfits were done extremely well, and I highly appreciate them.

[b]INTERFACE:[/b]
A nice, smooth interface for the new TABS. And i love it!

[b]Now on to the negatives.[/b] (Yes, you may have noticed I haven't covered the new units but I will get to that later)

[h1]CRASHING:[/h1]
The game crashes every now and then, although this is to be expected for Early Access games.

[b]NO HELP:[/b]
For new players, there is no help for controls. Although basic controls are rather easy to get a hang of, more 'advanced' controls such as 'f' for fly-around camera (before match starts) and slow-mo controls (left-click and g) are not pointed out to you. Maybe a basic tutorial might help here?

[b]SUPERLAG:[/b]
Super laggy when doing a large-scale battle, only not laggy if you have it constantly on slow-motion.

Now onto my biggest dislike/positive. NEW UNITS!!

[h1][b]NEW UNITS:[/b][/h1]
So there are tonnes of new units added (such as the entire cavemen faction) but there were also tonnes of units taken out. Some personal favourites include:
- Ninjas and Grand Master Ninjas
- Samurais
- Super and Dark Peasants
- Muskets
- Whole entire Neon faction
- The guy that spawns chickens
Now where did these all go??
I hope they come back again, but it was kind of a disappointment when I first opened the game and realised they weren't there. Also other units showcased in videos upcoming to the full release weren't released either. Some of these I was also really looking forward to messing around with, such as the Flamethrower and DaVinci Tank.
I understand that some things won't make the cut, but...

In conclusion there are multiple negatives to the game, however there is many positive aspects as well. I hope in the coming updates that these units will be added and the crash bug fixed.

All in all for the price, it's def. worth it.

🎯 Gameplay Overview
Totally Accurate Battle Simulator (TABS) is a physics-based tactics game and a completely chaotic battle simulator developed by Landfall. The game puts you in the role of the ultimate strategist, where the main goal is to place two armies of "wobblers" (gelatinous and unbalanced soldiers) on a battlefield and watch them fight in the most absurd ways possible. It features an extensive campaign mode where you must solve tactical scenarios within a limited budget, an entirely free Sandbox mode, and a highly detailed Unit Creator where you can build your own custom fighters and ridiculous factions.
👍 PROS:
• The ragdoll physics system delivers hilarious, purely random moments; no two battles ever feel or play out the same.
• Massive variety of historical, mythological, and fantasy units, further expanded by an active Steam Workshop full of community creations.
• The Unit Creator gives you almost absolute freedom to customize abilities, clothing, and stats for uniquely bizarre armies.
👎 CONS:
• Soldier AI is intentionally dumb, which can occasionally become frustrating when a powerful unit gets stuck on the map geometry.
• Advanced campaign levels can feel a bit repetitive, often being easily solved by simply spamming the same efficient unit type.

The samurai, his red armor glinting in the last dying rays of sunlight, shifts his stance. With a barely perceptible movement of his wrists, his blade describes a crescent in the frozen air. And then the samurai crouches, and in an instant he's among the archers, laying about himself with his blade, the cacophony of steel crashing against steel mingling with grunts of pain and screams of surprise. The archers realize too late that their foe is no mere samurai, but a shogun — a powerful feudal lord. Three archers stand, then two. One pierces the shogun's shoulder with a lucky shot, but an answering katana blow strikes him dead before he can celebrate. The last remaining archer, whose head is the size of a grapefruit and whose bow is held behind his back as though he's hiding a present from a toddler, looses an arrow that, predictably, does nothing. A flash of steel leaves him sprawling.

The shogun's breath fogs in the air. He turns limply toward the nearby forest and trudges forward, the arrow in his shoulder a painful memorial to the blue archer's death. There will be more killing before the night is through.

TLDR Very fun game if you like to mess around, but can have lot of strategy at times with Its 60+ different units.

The idea of the game is that you build an army from a very large selection of troops, which cost different amounts to fill a budget, in order to defeat the enemies. All of the levels (the ones I have played) seem hard at first but all give you a sense of enjoyment when you beat them, either using a wacky strategy where you pile all of one troop or using careful placement and army composition.

Units

The different units are separated into 9 different factions, (Tribal, Farmer, Medieval, Viking, Ancient, Renaissance, Dynasty, Pirate and Spooky), which all feel very different. For example: The Medieval faction focuses on very good all round units such as their knights which have good armour and damage, whereas the Viking faction focuses on high damage attacks like the berserker which has a large leap and strong axes. Overall, all of the factions deliver the same core ingredients, but do it in different ways. The AI is what you think it would be judging by the games sense of humour. A lot of the units will sometimes ragdoll in the middle of battle or get stuck under a pile of other troops, which makes for entertaining battles.

Maps

In each level, there is a selected map that fits with the theme of the level. Each faction has its own map(s) which fit with its theme. For example: the dynasty map is filled with temples, cherry blossoms and statues, focusing on multiple paths and a large pit in the centre, The polar opposite to this map is Medieval 2, which has a large open field in front of a large castle, which makes for good army composition strategies.

The simulation mode

This mode is about creating the most havoc or trying out a new combo of troops. You select from a regular map or a test one with different obstacles like a maze or a large arena. They feel like they are built to mess around, which is really fun in this game. In this mode you have infinite money, so it encourages you to try battles like 10 Zeuses vs 100 halflings.

The first person control

This mode is entirely optional but I think adds a new element of strategy to the game, allowing you to control a units movements and attacks, allowing you to prioritise all of your archers to defeat the ballista before the sheildmen. For example on the map Medieval 1 there are two fields connected by a large bridge. In this battle I was up against a large group of squires, basic swordsmen. I had quite limited money, so I was encouraged to do something new. I used a group of farmers to distract the squires and keep them busy while I controlled a harvester unit, which has a large scythe. I walked to the edge of the bridge with my back to a pillar. Once the farmers were all dead, I waited for the squires to walk round the pillar, a few at a time I hooked them with my scythe and swung away from the bridge, tossing them into the water, instantly downing them. I continued this until i won. This added control just adds icing on the cake.

The secrets (Spoiler warning)

[spoiler] The way this game does secrets is very unique. All of the secrets are units which are found in the secret tab when selecting troops for battle. They all follow one of the factions, and are often very interesting in their attacks and AI. For example the cheerleader tribal unit reduces another units cooldowns on their attacks, so stacking twenty of them with a ballista becomes a viable, but expensive strategy. The shouter is a viking unit which can shout, stunning a large group of enemy troops. The way you unlock all of the troops is by loading up a map, pressing the F key to free the camera and fly round the map, if you can find weapons hidden in different places you unlock the troops. [/spoiler].

Steam workshop

The inclusion of a level editor is amazing as you never run out of levels, you can just easily download and play community made levels. Or you can make and share your own.

The Cons

If your computer isn't very strong it can lag a lot and sometimes crash when you pile 100 units on top of each other. The only thing the devs could do to improve is Keep adding more features.

If you enjoy strategy and army-building with some comedy, get this game.
